title: Aromatic Moroccan Chicken Tagine
description: Jammy, silky Moroccan chicken tagine that showcases fresh thyme and a shio-koji cure, all while staying low-fat.
instructions: Season the chicken with ground cumin, smoked paprika, dried thyme, cinnamon, ginger and black pepper, then let it rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and brown the chicken thighs skin side down until golden, about 4 minutes.
Turn the chicken over, add sliced onion and minced garlic, and cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
Sprinkle fresh thyme and add the preserved lemon slices, then pour in the low-sodium chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Stir in shio-koji and honey, then cover the pot and let it cook over low heat for 35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce thickens.
Add the carrot chunks and sliced olives, cover again, and cook for an additional 10 minutes so the vegetables absorb the flavors.
Check that the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) before serving.
Serve the tagine hot over a smear of low-fat yogurt or a small portion of couscous if desired.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
